issue.title: Cursor pagination silently drops rows when sorting by a nullable column
issue.body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?
Airflow Core

### Apache Airflow version
`main` (and any released 3.x line that ships cursor pagination; affected code in `airflow/api_fastapi/common/cursors.py`)

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

The public REST list endpoints `GET .../dagRuns` and `GET .../taskInstances`, when paginated with `cursor` and sorted by a **nullable** column (`start_date`, `end_date`, `duration`, `run_after`), **silently drop rows** — no error. When the column has `NULL`s and the result spans more than one page, every row on one side of the NULL/non-NULL boundary is never returned.

**All backends are affected** — which side vanishes flips with NULL ordering: SQLite/MySQL `ASC` (and Postgres `DESC`) drop the **non-NULL** rows; the reverse drops the **NULL** rows.

Reproduction (self-contained, uses the real pagination helpers):

```python
from sqlalchemy import create_engine, Integer, String, Column, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base, Session
from airflow.api_fastapi.common.parameters import SortParam
from airflow.api_fastapi.common.cursors import encode_cursor, apply_cursor_filter

Base = declarative_base()

class M(Base):
    __tablename__ = "m"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    val = Column(String, nullable=True)   # nullable sort column, e.g. start_date

eng = create_engine("sqlite://")
Base.metadata.create_all(eng)
with Session(eng) as s:
    s.add_all([M(id=i, val=v) for i, v in [(1, None), (2, None), (3, None), (4, "a"), (5, "b"), (6, "c")]])
    s.commit()

sort = SortParam(allowed_attrs=["val"], model=M); sort.set_value(["val"])  # ORDER BY val ASC
returned, token = [], None
with Session(eng) as s:
    while True:
        stmt = sort.to_orm(select(M)).limit(2)
        if token is not None:
            stmt = apply_cursor_filter(stmt, token, sort)
        rows = s.scalars(stmt).all()
        if not rows:
            break
        returned.extend(m.id for m in rows)
        token = encode_cursor(rows[-1], sort)

print(returned)   # [1, 2, 3]  -> rows 4, 5, 6 silently dropped
```

`ASC` returns `[1, 2, 3]` (rows 4,5,6 missing); `DESC` drops `[1, 2, 3]`.

**Root cause** (`airflow/api_fastapi/common/cursors.py`): for a `NULL` cursor value, `_nested_keyset_predicate` reduces to `col IS NULL AND pk > pk_value` — the `col IS NOT NULL` branch meant to cross the boundary is dead. Non-NULL comparisons are also `UNKNOWN` for NULL rows, so pagination never crosses the boundary from either side. And `SortParam.to_orm` emits a plain `ASC`/`DESC` (no `NULLS FIRST/LAST`), so NULL position is the dialect default the predicate can't match.

### What you think should happen instead?

Every matching row returned exactly once, regardless of NULLs or backend. A fix needs the `ORDER BY` and the keyset predicate to agree on a deterministic NULL placement — e.g. an explicit null-rank sort key also encoded in the cursor — which would make NULL ordering consistent across dialects (a behavior change on some dialects, worth discussing).

### Operating System
Any — backend-dependent, not OS-dependent.

### Deployment
Other (local reproduction; not deployment-specific).

### Versions of Apache Airflow Providers
Not applicable (airflow-core).

### Official Helm Chart version
Not Applicable

### Anything else?
Happens every time the conditions hold; silent, so clients (UIs, scripts, exports) can't tell rows are missing.
